AggregateBucket.description:
One group in an enumerated aggregate (retrieval §9): a key and its count.

`key` is the group label — a predicate, an object entity, a timeline
period, or an entity id rendered as text — and `null` for the single
bucket of a plain count. `entity_id` is populated when the group IS an
entity (group-by-object, delta-top-entities, typed-absence), so the
agent can hop straight to it without re-resolving the label.
AggregateBucket.title: AggregateBucket

AggregateReport.description:
An enumerated aggregate's result: the form asked, and its buckets.

Aggregation is enumerated, never general (retrieval §9): each `form`
is a bounded SQL shape with a predictable cost. `total` is the sum
across buckets (or the single count); `bounded_by` names the cap when
the shape rides a bounded feed (e.g. delta-top-entities), so a reader
knows the ranking is over the window, not all of history.
AggregateReport.title: AggregateReport

AsOfTemporalScope.description: A two-axis audit read with an explicitly reconstructed identity regime.
AsOfTemporalScope.title: AsOfTemporalScope

AtTemporalScope.description: A current-belief read of the world-valid state at one instant.
AtTemporalScope.title: AtTemporalScope

CapabilityReadiness.description: One live capability's required/readiness state and safe reason.
CapabilityReadiness.title: CapabilityReadiness

ChangeRecord.description:
One entry in the `delta` change feed (S13/S14/S30).

`kind` is what changed (relation | observation | claim | page) and
`change` is how (new | invalidated | capped | recompiled). `at` is the
instant that placed it in the feed — the ingestion, invalidation, or
recompilation time the caller's `since` was compared against — so a
follow-up `delta` can resume from the last `at` it saw.
ChangeRecord.title: ChangeRecord

ChunkEvidenceResult.description: One live source chunk, distinct from an extracted claim or fact.
ChunkEvidenceResult.title: ChunkEvidenceResult

CoMember.description:
One other side of a contradiction, surfaced with the fact (S23).

A light record — enough to see the competing claim and hydrate it — so a
contradiction block can carry several sides without recursion.
CoMember.title: CoMember

ContextBundleV1.description: The sole side-by-side response for complete testimony and fact reads.
ContextBundleV1.title: ContextBundleV1

Contradiction.description:
The S23 contract block: a fact's live contradiction, never one-sided.

Returning one side of a live contradiction group without its others is a
contract violation, not a ranking choice ("contradictions are surfaced,
never silently resolved"). The bounded form: co-members come back INLINE
up to a guaranteed cap (typical groups are 2–3 sides — both FY2023
revenue figures together, each with its own evidence handle); beyond the
cap the block still always carries `group_id`, `returned`, `total`, and a
`continuation`. One-sided is never a valid answer.
Contradiction.title: Contradiction

CurrentTemporalScope.description: A read evaluated against the world and identity state at one instant.
CurrentTemporalScope.title: CurrentTemporalScope

DeploymentBuildInfo.description:
Non-secret identity of the code and model bindings currently serving.

Available without version ids so a caller can verify provenance *before*
submitting work, rather than after the pipeline has already processed it
under whatever image happened to be running.

build_revision.description: Source revision stamped into the running image at build time; empty when the image was built without it.
build_revision.title: Build Revision

document_binding_generation.description: Current document-local entity binding projection generation.
document_binding_generation.title: Document Binding Generation

DeploymentBuildInfo.title: DeploymentBuildInfo

DocumentPage.description:
One page of the document inventory.

``cursor`` is opaque and absent on the last page. Callers must not
construct one: it encodes the sort position, and an invented value would
silently skip or repeat documents rather than fail.
DocumentPage.title: DocumentPage

DocumentSummary.description:
One document lineage, with the newest snapshot the engine has observed.

``latest`` is the highest ``version_no`` in the lineage, which is
deliberately not the same as the lineage's *current* version. The current
pointer only moves once a snapshot finishes processing, so a document
whose first version is still converting — or whose newest version failed —
has no current version at all. Keying this on the current pointer would
make exactly the documents somebody is worried about disappear from the
list, which is the opposite of what an intake view is for.

``serving`` says whether a *ready* snapshot exists to answer questions
from, so the two facts stay separable: "the newest upload failed" and
"there is nothing here to search" are different situations and a customer
needs to tell them apart.
DocumentSummary.title: DocumentSummary

DocumentVersionSummary.description:
The state of one observed snapshot of a document.

``status`` is the version's own processing state, not a judgement about
the document: a lineage whose newest version is ``failed`` may still be
serving an older one that is ``ready``.
DocumentVersionSummary.title: DocumentVersionSummary

EntityCandidate.description: One ranked resolve candidate (never a silent guess, S51).
EntityCandidate.title: EntityCandidate

Envelope.description:
The D49 envelope: results plus the answer's machine-readable self-account.

Each answer is one operation's cohesive typed result. Independent complete
testimony and fact responses use ``ContextBundleV1`` instead of nesting or
blending payloads inside an envelope.
Envelope.title: Envelope

EvidenceResult.description: One evidence-grain record: a claim with its provenance anchors.
EvidenceResult.title: EvidenceResult

EvidenceTotal.description: Exact evidence disclosure for one fact and one evidence stance.
EvidenceTotal.title: EvidenceTotal

FactEvidence.description: One explicit fact-to-claim association in a flat compound answer.
FactEvidence.title: FactEvidence

FactResult.description: One fact-grain record: a live relation or observation, hydrated.
FactResult.title: FactResult

FactSupport.description:
Whether a fact still has current-testimony support (D54).

`current` is the normal state; `withdrawn` means every source that
asserted the fact has stopped (an open `support_withdrawn` review flag) —
the fact is *flagged, not vanished*, so an agent sees the ground moved
before planning against it. A withdrawn fact is still returned.
FactSupport.title: FactSupport

Freshness.description:
Per-source freshness stamps (S42): what lag the answer could carry.

Each contributing channel also exposes its **`believed_at` horizon**: the
oldest system-time a query can reach before the channel can no longer
answer. Whenever a horizon is finite, a `believed_at` before it must return
a `boundary` (retrieval §3), never a silent truncation. The live graph has
no separate freshness stamp because it reads the same PostgreSQL snapshot.
Freshness.title: Freshness

Grain.description: The D49 grain type-system: what kind of truth a result is.
Grain.title: Grain

GraphEdge.description: One traversed relation, carrying its bi-temporal state.
GraphEdge.title: GraphEdge

GraphInvocation.description: One graph helper's terminal work and truncation disclosure.
GraphInvocation.title: GraphInvocation

GraphNode.description: One entity the traversal reached, with its hop distance.
GraphNode.title: GraphNode

GraphPath.description:
One connection between two entities — a COMPOUND result.

A path revalidates as a unit (S17/S21): if hydration drops any edge,
the whole path drops, because a path with a hole is not a shorter
path — it is a different (and false) claim about connection.
GraphPath.title: GraphPath

HistoryTemporalScope.description: All currently believed fact intervals that began by evaluation time.
HistoryTemporalScope.title: HistoryTemporalScope

IdentityRegime.description:
Which identity boundary answered a read (S61).

`current` (the default) follows today's aliases and merge redirects even
under a past `believed_at`; `as_of` means the identity boundary was
reconstructed as it stood at the queried instant (the transcript-based
`examples.identity_as_of` saved query). The envelope always states which, so an audit
read can never silently mix today's identities with yesterday's beliefs.
IdentityRegime.title: IdentityRegime

IngestedVersion.description:
What one ingest did: the lineage/version it landed on, and whether it was new.

`created=False` is the D55 content-hash no-op: identical bytes re-ingested
never create a second version or re-run the chain.
IngestedVersion.title: IngestedVersion

KFreshness.description:
The compiled-grain honesty block (retrieval §5): a K page's timestamp.

A compiled answer is pre-paid synthesis *with a timestamp*, so any answer
that consumed a K page carries when it compiled, whether it is stale
(inputs changed since), and how many evidence-change flags are still open
against it — the reader-facing flag surface (k_layers spike 9). An agent
sees "this page has 3 unresolved flags" before planning against it (S34).
KFreshness.title: KFreshness

Negative.description: One typed 'no': each kind demands a different agent reaction.
Negative.title: Negative

NegativeKind.description:
The fixed negative-answer taxonomy (S29/S39/S55).

Deliberately no `denied` kind: content-level authorization is a library
non-goal (retrieval §9), and hard-deleted (forgotten) content is
indistinguishable-from-never-existed (S55), so it surfaces as
`unknown_entity`/`known_empty`, never a distinct kind. Freezing the
taxonomy now is safe precisely because of these two omissions —
retrofitting a kind onto a deployed API breaks consumers.
NegativeKind.title: NegativeKind

OverlapTemporalScope.description: A current-belief read of facts overlapping one inclusive interval.
OverlapTemporalScope.title: OverlapTemporalScope

PageRef.description:
One K page the `pages_about` discovery index reports (S31/S45).

The rule-key inverted index that routes writes, read backwards: which
pages exist about an entity or key. `stale` mirrors the refresh state —
a page whose inputs changed but has not recompiled — so discovery never
presents an out-of-date page as fresh without saying so.
PageRef.title: PageRef

PipelineReadinessReport.description: Machine-verifiable E/P readiness for a bounded set of versions.

build_revision.description: Source revision stamped into the running image at build time. Empty when the image was built without it. Comparing this against the revision a benchmark prepared with is the only way to know the serving code is the code under test; a filesystem checkout says nothing about what the containers actually run.
build_revision.title: Build Revision

document_binding_generation.description: Current bounded document-entity projection generation. NULL means document-local exact T0 replay is disabled.
document_binding_generation.title: Document Binding Generation

model_bindings.description: Current non-secret serving-process configuration; this is not processing-time provenance for the requested versions.
model_bindings.title: Model Bindings

PipelineReadinessReport.title: PipelineReadinessReport

PipelineReadinessRequest.description: Exhaustive readiness capabilities for a bounded version set.
PipelineReadinessRequest.title: PipelineReadinessRequest

PipelineStageReadiness.description: One expected document-version stage at the public readiness boundary.
PipelineStageReadiness.title: PipelineStageReadiness

QueryErrorCode.description: Every public failure code, exactly as bound in design §4.1.
QueryErrorCode.title: QueryErrorCode

RankedItem.description:
One item in a fused or reranked ordering (retrieval §3: `fuse`/`rerank`).

`score` is the operator's output — the RRF sum for `fuse`, the signal
value for `rerank` — and the tuple order IS the rank. `signals` keeps
each contributing value visible, because the rerankers are meant to be
inspectable stages (D9), not a black-box sort.
RankedItem.title: RankedItem

ReadinessRequirements.description: The exhaustive capability set a readiness caller may require.
ReadinessRequirements.title: ReadinessRequirements

ResultColumn.description: One projected column: name, SQL type, nullability.
ResultColumn.title: ResultColumn

ResultLimits.description: The caps this request actually ran under.
ResultLimits.title: ResultLimits

SearchRequest.description:
A search, with the terms in the body rather than the request line.

The query is the customer's own words — often the most sensitive string in
the whole exchange. A URL is not a private place: it is written to access
logs, kept by proxies, retained in browser history, and attached to
referrers. So the search surface takes a body, and the terms never appear
in a request line (D59).

The ``GET`` forms remain for existing clients, which reach the deployment
over a private path. A browser does not.
SearchRequest.title: SearchRequest

SemanticInvocation.description: One §3.4 nomination invocation's disclosure (populated by Batch C).
SemanticInvocation.title: SemanticInvocation

SourceRecord.description: One hydrated source document handle (S5: down to the artifact URI).
SourceRecord.title: SourceRecord

SqlExplainRequest.description: Body for `POST /query/sql/explain` — sql and parameters only.
SqlExplainRequest.title: SqlExplainRequest

ToolDescriptor.description: One assured operation and its live implementation identity.
ToolDescriptor.title: ToolDescriptor

TranscriptEntry.description:
One append-only decision record, as the `transcript` primitive returns it.

The audit trail is uniform across the four subjects a decision can be
about (S8/S32/S35): a supersession-adjudicated relation or observation,
a resolved/merged entity, or a compiled K page. `subject_kind` says
which, and `related_id` points at the counterpart the decision paired
the subject with — the other relation/observation in a supersede pair,
the entity absorbed in a merge, or the compilation's artifact — so an
agent can walk from any decision to what it acted on.
TranscriptEntry.title: TranscriptEntry

Truncation.title: Truncation

Validity.description: A result's bi-temporal state as hydration re-read it (D48).
Validity.title: Validity

VersionPipelineReadiness.description: The complete expected continuous pipeline state for one version.
VersionPipelineReadiness.title: VersionPipelineReadiness

get.description: Report which code and model bindings are serving, before any work.

One page of documents, newest lineage first.

Ordered by when each document was *first seen*, which never changes —
re-ingesting one does not move it up. An activity order would, and a
keyset cursor against a moving key drops and repeats rows.

`status` filters on the *newest* version's state, which is what makes
"show me what failed" answerable in one call rather than by paging the
whole corpus and filtering client-side.

Return bounded equal-length shortest paths between two entities.

get.description: The S5 chain: relation → evidence claims → source documents.

post.description:
Push one file through E0, optionally as a stable lineage version.

Attribution travels in **headers, never the query string**: the
reference is erasable PII and a URL is copied verbatim into access
logs, proxies and traces, where a later principal deletion cannot
reach it.

The pair is honoured only when the composing profile declares its
perimeter trusted (``trusted_principal_source``). The deployment-wide
bearer identifies a deployment, not a caller, so elsewhere any client
could assert it was a person. Untrusted attribution is **ignored, not
rejected**: nothing forged is recorded either way, and refusing would
let a metadata concern fail an otherwise valid ingest.

parameters.description: One of: user | api_credential | service. Sent with X-Ingest-Principal-Ref. Ignored unless the deployment declares a trusted principal source; malformed values are 422 only on a trusted deployment.

post.description:
Run one assured operation by name over JSON arguments.

The route-level table cannot classify this one: operations are registry
data, and whether a given operation mutates is a property of the
operation rather than of the path. So the scope check happens here,
against the descriptor, and an operation that has not declared itself
non-mutating is refused to a read-only credential.
